text: Hx: مريض ذكر يبلغ من العمر 28 عاماً، يراجع العيادة بسبب ظهور نمو جلدي خشن ومتقرن حول ظفر الإبهام في اليد اليمنى منذ شهرين. ينفي وجود أي آفات مشابهة على باطن القدمين. Ex: لوحظ وجود ورم حليمي متقرن يحيط بحافة الظفر، مع وجود نقاط سوداء صغيرة نتيجة تخثر الأوعية الدموية الدقيقة. لا توجد آفات في أماكن أخرى من الجسم. Imp: ثؤلول حول الظفر (Periungual wart). Plan: Doctor: سأقوم بوضع محلول حمض الساليسيليك الموضعي مع تغطية المنطقة بشريط لاصق. Patient: هل أحتاج إلى عملية جراحية؟ Doctor: لا، سنبدأ بالعلاج الموضعي وسنرى النتائج في المراجعة القادمة بعد أسبوعين. تجنب العبث بالمنطقة أو قضم الجلد المحيط بالظفر.

Doctor: Good morning, Mr. Henderson. I have the results of your neck biopsy. The pathology shows a poorly differentiated carcinoma of the thyroid. It is not as slow-growing as papillary or follicular types, but it is not as aggressive as an undifferentiated or anaplastic tumor. It is distinct from medullary cancer since the cells don't show neuroendocrine features. Patient: That sounds serious. Is it going to spread quickly? Doctor: It is a mid-range, aggressive cancer, which is why we need to move fast. Vitals today are stable: BP 130/82, HR 76, Temp 98.6 F. On exam, the neck mass remains firm and fixed at the right lobe, about 3cm in size. Your vocal cords appear normal, and there is no evidence of airway obstruction right now. Plan: We need to schedule a total thyroidectomy followed by radioactive iodine treatment. I am referring you to endocrine surgery today. We will also order a CT of your chest and neck to ensure the lymph nodes are clear. Do you have questions about the surgery?

Pt, 28yo M, presents for routine f/u of known Factor VII deficiency. Asymptomatic, no hx of bruising, epistaxis, or abnormal bleeding. Labs show stable low activity levels. PE unremarkable. DX: Congenital FVII deficiency, asymptomatic. Plan: No intervention needed, continue routine monitoring, no ASA/NSAIDs, return prn if symptoms occur.

Paciente, 34a, relata início de dispneia, sibilância e edema facial logo após inalar pólen em jardim. SV: PA 90/60, FC 115, SatO2 91%. EF: angioedema labial, broncoespasmo difuso, sem lesões cutâneas. Dx: Anafilaxia por inalação de alérgeno (pólen). Conduta: IM adrenalina, salbutamol nebulizado, observação rigorosa. Doctor: Sente aperto no peito? Patient: Sim, comecei a tossir e inchar depois de cheirar aquelas flores.

Doctor: Good morning, Leo. I have reviewed your blood work and the specialized metabolic panel we ordered. Your symptoms of recurring episodic nausea and the finding of persistent high levels of glycerol in your urine, alongside your normal blood sugar and lactate levels, help clarify what is going on. Patient: I have been worried about these episodes, especially since they do not seem tied to specific meals. Does this mean it is a problem with how my body breaks down sugar? Doctor: Not exactly. This is specifically a disorder of glycerol metabolism. Your body is struggling to convert glycerol into the energy pathways it usually follows, which leads to an accumulation of these compounds in your system. It is distinct from issues with glycogen or galactose processing because your liver enzymes related to those are perfectly normal. We are going to start you on a specialized low-fat diet to reduce the glycerol load and schedule a follow-up with the metabolic geneticist to confirm the exact enzymatic deficiency. Vitals today show a BP of 122/80, pulse 74, and temp 98.6. Findings confirm the elevated urinary glycerol excretion. We will monitor your symptoms closely as we adjust your intake.

Doctor: Jambo mama, leo unajisikiaje? Patient: Sijisikii vizuri daktari. Nasahau mambo mengi sana siku hizi, hata majina ya wajukuu wangu. Doctor: Pole sana. Hebu tuangalie shinikizo la damu. Vitals: BP 130/85, Pulse 76, Temp 36.6. Uchunguzi wa kimwili unaonyesha umakini mdogo lakini moyo na mapafu ni safi. Patient: Je, huu ni uzee tu au kuna tatizo kubwa? Doctor: Kutokana na mazungumzo yetu na vipimo vya kumbukumbu, inaonekana una hali inayoitwa ugonjwa wa Alzheimer ambao unasababisha kupungua kwa uwezo wa kufikiri na kukumbuka. Hii ni hali ambayo ubongo hupoteza uwezo wake taratibu. Patient: Hiyo ina maana gani kwa maisha yangu ya baadaye? Doctor: Tutaanza dawa za kusaidia utulivu na kuboresha utendaji wa ubongo. Pia, ni muhimu sana uwe na msaidizi nyumbani na ufanye mazoezi mepesi ya akili kila siku. Tutapanga kurudi baada ya wiki mbili kuona jinsi unavyoendelea na dawa hizi mpya. Nitakuandikia rufaa kwa mtaalamu wa neva ili tuchunguze zaidi hali yako.

3yo M w/ known PHOX2B mutation presents for F/U. No obesity or hypothalamic dysfunction noted. Polysom confirms persistent central alveolar hypoventilation onset at birth during sleep. Currently stable on nocturnal NPPV. Plan: cont. vent support, repeat titration study in 6mo, monitor for autonomic dysregulation. Dx: Congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.

Doctor: Good morning, Sarah. I have reviewed the records from your emergency room visit last week where you lost consciousness and had some involuntary shaking. How are you feeling today? Patient: I am still a bit shaken up, honestly. I don't remember much of the event, just waking up on the floor. I have never had this happen before. Doctor: Based on the witness reports and the neurological exam today, it sounds like you experienced a sudden electrical disturbance in your brain. We are not seeing any signs of trauma or electrolyte issues that would explain this. Because this occurred unexpectedly and without an identified external cause, I am classifying this as an episode of seizure activity. We do not have enough information yet to categorize it further, so we will label this as epilepsy or seizures, unspecified, for now. Vitals: Blood pressure 122/78, pulse 72, temp 98.6 F. Findings: Patient is alert and oriented x3. Cranial nerves are intact, reflexes symmetric, no focal deficits noted. Plan: We need to order an EEG to look for abnormal electrical patterns and an MRI of your brain. Please refrain from driving until we get these results back and clear you for safety.

Pt reports chronic intermittent horizontal diplopia, worse at distance. Exam shows orthophoria at near, but significant esotropia on primary gaze distance testing that worsens with attempted abduction. Full range of motion, no neurological deficits. Dx: Synergistic divergence. Plan: Fresnel prism for distance activities and monitor q6mo.

Doctor: Good morning, Sarah. I reviewed your scan, and it confirms my suspicion. You have a superior canal dehiscence syndrome. Basically, there is a tiny hole in the bone overlying the superior semicircular canal of your inner ear. Patient: Is that why I hear my own heartbeat and my voice echoes in my head? Doctor: Exactly. That is called autophony. Because the bony cover is missing, internal sounds amplify, and loud external noises like a door slamming actually trigger dizziness. This differs from Meniere’s because you do not have the classic fluctuating hearing loss or fullness, and unlike BPPV, your symptoms are pressure-induced rather than just position-induced. Vitals: BP 125/80, HR 72, Temp 98.6. Exam: Weber test lateralizes to the affected left ear. Fistula test positive for eye movement. Plan: We will avoid heavy lifting and Valsalva maneuvers for now. I am referring you to neuro-otology to discuss potential surgical resurfacing of the canal since the dehiscence is clinically significant and affecting your daily life. Avoid loud environments in the interim.

Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gable. I have reviewed the results of your echocardiogram and your recent blood work. How have you been feeling since we last spoke? Patient: Honestly, Doctor, I am still so winded when I walk to the mailbox. I feel like I just cannot get enough air, and my ankles are still swollen by the evening. Doctor: I hear you. Based on the imaging and your symptoms of shortness of breath and fluid retention, it is clear that your heart muscle is struggling to pump blood effectively to the rest of your body. Your left ventricle is not functioning properly, which is causing this backup. We call this left ventricular failure. I need to get you started on a new medication regimen to manage this fluid and support your heart's workload. Vitals today show blood pressure is 145/90 and your pulse is 88. Plan: We will start lisinopril and furosemide today. Please monitor your daily weights, eat a low-sodium diet, and follow up in two weeks for repeat labs to ensure your kidneys are handling the medications well.

Pt: 42yo M, welder by trade, presents with acute respiratory distress following accidental exposure to unknown chemical vapors in an unventilated workspace yesterday. Hx of non-smoker, no prior asthma. Currently reports persistent cough, mild chest tightness, and a scratchy throat. PE: BP 138/86, HR 92, RR 20, SpO2 95% on RA. Lungs: diminished air entry at bases, no wheezes or rales noted. Oropharynx: mild diffuse erythema, no edema. Imp: Respiratory status decline consistent with inhalation of unidentified industrial gas/fumes. Plan: 1. Monitor O2 saturation closely. 2. Start bronchodilator trial to assess for reactive airway response. 3. Advise strict avoidance of workplace until air quality assessment is complete. 4. Follow up in 48 hours for repeat PFTs. 5. Discuss proper PPE and ventilation safety protocols.

Doctor: नमस्ते, आप आज कैसा महसूस कर रहे हैं? Patient: डॉक्टर साहब, पिछले कुछ हफ्तों से पेट में लगातार मरोड़ उठ रही है और मुझे बार-बार दस्त हो रहे हैं। वजन भी काफी कम हो गया है और बहुत कमजोरी महसूस होती है। Doctor: आपकी रिपोर्ट और लक्षणों को देखकर मुझे लगता है कि यह क्रोहन रोग है। यह एक पुरानी सूजन संबंधी स्थिति है जो आपके पाचन तंत्र के किसी भी हिस्से को प्रभावित कर सकती है। यह आपके मामले में पाचन नली के विभिन्न हिस्सों में सूजन पैदा कर रही है। आपकी धड़कन 82 प्रति मिनट है और रक्तचाप 120/80 mmHg है, जो सामान्य है। पेट को दबाने पर कोमलता महसूस हो रही है। Patient: क्या यह ठीक हो पाएगा? Doctor: इसे पूरी तरह खत्म करना मुश्किल है, लेकिन हम दवाओं से सूजन को नियंत्रित कर सकते हैं ताकि आप सामान्य जीवन जी सकें। मैं आपको कुछ एंटी-इंफ्लेमेटरी दवाएं लिख रहा हूं और हमें नियमित रूप से आपकी स्थिति की निगरानी करनी होगी। आपको आहार में बदलाव करने होंगे और अधिक मसालेदार भोजन से बचना होगा। क्या आपको कोई और परेशानी है? Patient: जी नहीं, समझ गया। धन्यवाद डॉक्टर।

Paciente: Varón de 45 años consulta por lesiones cutáneas persistentes. Hx: Refiere aparición de manchas anulares con borde elevado y queratósico en extremidades inferiores desde hace varios años. Sin antecedentes de relevancia. Ex: Al examen físico, se observan múltiples placas eritematosas con un borde periférico elevado de aspecto ligeramente surcado (coronoide) en ambas piernas. No se palpan adenopatías. Vitals: TA 120/80 mmHg, FC 72 lpm, Temp 36.6°C. Imp: Poroceratosis actínica superficial diseminada. La presencia del característico borde en cresta (lamela coronoide) en la biopsia superficial confirma el diagnóstico, diferenciándolo de otras queratodermias. Plan: Se solicita interconsulta con Dermatología para crioterapia y se recomienda fotoprotección estricta. Doctor: "Las lesiones parecen ser poroceratosis, una condición donde la capa externa de la piel crece de forma irregular creando esos bordes que siente al tacto". Paciente: "¿Debo preocuparme por si se vuelven malignas?" Doctor: "Es infrecuente, pero requiere vigilancia periódica para evitar complicaciones y mejorar la apariencia estética".

Doctor: المريضة طفلة 8 سنوات، تعاني من آلام وتيبس صباحي بالمفاصل منذ 3 أشهر، حرارة 37.2، نبض 85. تورم خفيف بمفاصل متعددة دون تحديد نمط معين، لا توجد طفح جلدي أو أعراض جهازية. التشخيص: التهاب مفاصل مجهول السبب عند الأطفال غير محدد. Patient: أشعر بوجع شديد في ركبتي ومعصمي عند الاستيقاظ.

Doctor: Hujambo, nini kinakuleta leo? Patient: Sijisikii vizuri daktari, nimegundua mkojo wangu una povu jingi sana siku hizi na miguu inavimba kidogo. Doctor: Sawa, hebu tuangalie vipimo vyako. Shinikizo la damu ni 130/85, uzito ni kilo 75. Vipimo vya maabara vinaonyesha protini inaendelea kutoka kwenye mkojo wako mara kwa mara, jambo ambalo si la kawaida. Patient: Je, hiyo inamaanisha nini daktari? Doctor: Hii inaashiria kuwa figo zako zinafanya kazi kwa shida na zinapitisha protini nyingi kwenye mkojo kwa muda mrefu sasa. Hali hii tunaiita protinuria ya kudumu ambayo haijabainishwa chanzo chake kamili, lakini figo hazichuji vizuri protini hiyo. Patient: Inatibika? Doctor: Ndio, tutaanza kwa kupunguza chumvi kwenye chakula na nitakuandikia dawa ya kusaidia kurekebisha shinikizo la damu ili kupunguza presha kwenye figo zako. Tutafanya vipimo vingine mwezi ujao kufuatilia kama hali inatulia. Unapaswa kuepuka dawa za maumivu za dukani zisizo na ushauri wa daktari kwani zinaweza kuongeza mzigo kwenye figo zako. Je, una swali lingine? Patient: Hapana, nimeelewa. Asante daktari.

34F, healthy. Pt reports primary sexual response previously normal, now unable to achieve orgasm during masturbation or with partner over last 6 mos. Sexual desire/arousal intact. No meds or psych hx. Findings suggest acquired situational lack of climax. Will trial sensate focus exercises and eval for relationship stressors. F/u 4 wks.

Pt: 28yo G2P1 at 34w gestation presents with worsening RUQ pain, N/V, and malaise. Hx: No prior HTN. Vitals: BP 162/104, HR 102, RR 18, SpO2 98%. Exam: Significant epigastric tenderness, 1+ pitting edema to mid-shin, hyperreflexia present. Labs: Platelets 88k, AST 180 U/L, ALT 210 U/L, LDH 750 U/L. UA shows 3+ proteinuria. Assessment: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count consistent with HELLP syndrome, distinguished from simple severe pre-eclampsia by the systemic microangiopathic hemolytic component and profound thrombocytopenia. Plan: Admit to L&D for maternal stabilization and immediate fetal delivery. Administer MgSO4 for seizure prophylaxis, initiate IV antihypertensives to maintain SBP <160, and order stat type and screen for potential platelet and FFP transfusion. Consult Maternal-Fetal Medicine and Neonatology for imminent preterm delivery planning.

Patient is a 1-day-old male infant born at 39 weeks gestation via elective primary lower segment cesarean section due to maternal request. No history of labor, breech presentation, instrument assistance, or fetal distress during the procedure. Vitals: HR 142, RR 48, Temp 36.8C, SpO2 98% on room air. Physical Exam: Infant is active and well-perfused. Anterior fontanelle soft and flat. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Heart rate regular, no murmurs. Abdomen soft, non-distended. Hips stable without click or clunk. Neurological exam reveals appropriate tone and primitive reflexes. Assessment: Newborn infant currently adjusting to the transition from an intrauterine environment following an uncomplicated surgical birth. No evidence of birth trauma or complications related to instrumental delivery or malpresentation. Plan: Continue routine newborn care including Vitamin K and Hep B vaccine. Encourage skin-to-skin and breastfeeding on demand. Monitor for jaundice and ensure adequate wet diapers. Discharge home with parents tomorrow if stable.

Paciente de 12 años acude por crecimiento excesivo y desproporcionado del dedo índice derecho desde nacimiento. Doctor: Se observa hipertrofia focal de falanges y tejidos blandos en el 2º dedo de la mano dcha, sin afectación de pies ni otros dedos. DX: Macrodactilia de falanges de la mano. Plan: Derivación a ortopedia pediátrica para evaluación de resección quirúrgica y epifisiodesis.

Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gable. I have your urine culture results back from your recent bout of dysuria. Patient: Thanks, Doc. I just want to make sure we clear this up for good. Doctor: So, the lab identified E. coli as the culprit. Interestingly, the testing shows that this particular strain is fully susceptible to cephalosporins, penicillins, and carbapenems. It is not an ESBL producer, so we have plenty of options. However, the report confirms it is resistant to Ciprofloxacin and Levofloxacin. Patient: Does that mean the stuff I tried last week won't work? Doctor: Exactly. That is why your symptoms didn't improve. Since it is a fluoroquinolone resistant E. coli, we need to switch you to a different class of antibiotics entirely. I am going to start you on a cephalosporin based on these sensitivity profiles. Vital signs today are stable, temp 98.6, pulse 76, BP 122/80. Plan: Discontinue current fluoroquinolone, begin Cephalexin 500mg BID for seven days, and follow up in one week to ensure resolution of urinary frequency.

Patient: गरम तेल पैर पर गिर गया। Doctor: बाएँ पैर का निचला हिस्सा पूरी तरह जल गया है, त्वचा सफेद और सुन्न है, मांसपेशी तक क्षति है। निदान: बाएँ पैर का गहरा जटिल जलना। उपचार: घाव की सफाई, ड्रेसिंग, दर्द निवारक और सर्जिकल रेफरल।

Pt here for mandatory employer-req serum alc/tox screen per post-offer protocols. No injuries, no accident, no legal mandate. Vitals: BP 120/80, HR 72, temp 98.6F. Exam: AOx3, neuro intact, no signs of intoxication. Plan: Perform venipuncture for serum ethanol and comprehensive tox panel. Pt to follow up with HR for results.

Paciente 54a, sexo masc. Queixa de disfagia progressiva e constipação crônica grave. Exame: megacólon visível, ausculta cardíaca normal, sem sinais de ICC. Vitals: PA 120/80, FC 72. Hipótese: doença de Chagas com acometimento digestivo. Conduta: solicitar manometria esofágica, enema opaco e sorologia p/ T. cruzi. Retorno c/ resultados.

Doctor: Good morning, Mr. Henderson. I have reviewed your biopsy results from the bronchial brushing. Patient: I am worried, doc. What are we looking at? Doctor: The pathology report confirms a high-grade neuroendocrine malignancy known as small cell lung carcinoma. Given your extensive history of smoking, the rapid growth pattern we saw on the CT scan, and the central location of the mass near the main airways, this fits the profile of small cell over other types like adenocarcinoma or squamous cell. The cells are very small with scant cytoplasm, which is a hallmark of this aggressive subtype. Vitals today show a BP of 135/85, pulse 88, and O2 saturation 94% on room air. You are wheezing slightly, likely from that central obstruction. Patient: That sounds serious. What is the next move? Doctor: Because this type grows quickly and can spread early, we need to move fast. We will start you on systemic chemotherapy and prophylactic cranial irradiation to prevent spread to the brain. I am referring you to oncology immediately for staging and a port placement.

Doctor: Good morning, Leo. I have the results from your hematology workup. Based on the specific assays, it appears you have congenital afibrinogenemia. Patient: That sounds serious. Is that why I bleed so much when I get a cut? Doctor: Yes, your blood lacks a functional clotting protein called fibrinogen, which is Factor I. It is a specific hereditary issue. We checked your Factor X levels and vitamin K-dependent factors, and those were completely normal, so we can rule out those conditions. Your body simply isn't making enough of this base building block for clots. Vitals today show a blood pressure of 122/78 and heart rate of 72. Physical exam shows some mild bruising on your shins, but no active bleeding. Plan: We need to set up a prophylactic infusion schedule for the Factor I concentrate to keep your levels stable. I am referring you to the regional hemophilia center for ongoing management. We will repeat your fibrinogen activity levels in two weeks to see how your body responds to the baseline therapy. Please avoid any contact sports or aspirin-containing products moving forward to minimize your risk of internal bleeds.

Pt: 54yo F presents w/ 3mo hx of palpable purpura on LEs, persistent arthralgias in hands, and generalized malaise. Denies recent travel or drug use. PMH: Hep C (untreated). Vitals: T 98.4, BP 138/82, HR 76, RR 16, O2 sat 99%. Exam: Bilateral lower extremity non-blanching purpuric rash. Trace edema noted. Neuro: decreased pinprick sensation in distal feet. Labs: RF elevated, C4 low, positive cryoglobulins on testing. Assessment: Mixed cryoglobulinaemia, likely secondary to chronic HCV infection. Plan: 1. Confirm viral load and genotype for HCV. 2. Refer to rheumatology for assessment of vasculitic involvement. 3. Monitor renal function via BMP and UA for proteinuria. 4. Initiate counseling for upcoming antiviral therapy. Pt understands the need for systemic management to prevent nerve and kidney damage.

Pt presents w/ severe muscle weakness, hyporeflexia, and hypotension. Labs reveal serum Mg 3.8 mmol/L. History significant for recent excessive magnesium supplementation for constipation. Diagnosis: hypermagnesemia secondary to supplement overuse. Plan: discontinue Mg supplements, initiate IV NS hydration, and monitor cardiac rhythm until levels normalize.

Doctor: Buenos días, señora. Cuénteme, ¿cómo se ha sentido después del parto? Patient: Doctor, la verdad es que no me siento bien. Estoy muy triste todo el tiempo, lloro sin motivo y me siento abrumada con el bebé. No duermo aunque el niño descanse. Doctor: Entiendo perfectamente y le agradezco su sinceridad. Ha estado bajo mucha presión física y emocional recientemente. Tras revisar sus síntomas y lo que me cuenta, noto que está atravesando un cuadro de dificultades emocionales y mentales relacionadas con su reciente maternidad. No puedo darle un nombre específico todavía porque los síntomas se solapan, pero es claro que su salud mental se ha visto afectada tras el nacimiento de su hijo. Patient: ¿Es normal sentirse así? Tengo miedo de no ser una buena madre. Doctor: Es una situación que requiere atención, pero no está sola en esto. Vamos a iniciar un plan de apoyo psicológico semanal y evaluaremos si necesita medicación complementaria para estabilizar su estado de ánimo. Necesito que descanse y que su familia le ayude más en casa. ¿Le parece bien si nos vemos en una semana para ver cómo evoluciona?

Doctor: Bom dia, Sr. Carlos. Como o senhor tem se sentido desde que iniciamos o tratamento com CPAP para sua apneia obstrutiva? Patient: Doutor, estou usando a máscara toda noite, mas minha esposa diz que ainda percebo pausas respiratórias, mesmo com a pressão ajustada. Doctor: Interessante. Vamos revisar seus dados. O monitoramento mostra que, embora a obstrução tenha sido resolvida, você está apresentando episódios onde seu cérebro deixa de enviar o comando para respirar durante o sono, algo que não estava lá antes de usarmos a pressão positiva. Isso é uma apneia central induzida pelo próprio tratamento. Sinais vitais: PA 130/85, IMC 29, saturação 96%. Exame físico: orofaringe sem obstruções evidentes, pulmões limpos. O padrão de polissonografia não mostra Cheyne-Stokes nem sinais de insuficiência cardíaca. Plan: Vamos ajustar o nível de pressão da máquina para um modo adaptativo de servoventilação, pois seu sistema respiratório está reagindo de forma atípica à pressão fixa. Continuaremos monitorando mensalmente para ver se o cérebro se estabiliza. Volte em quatro semanas para nova leitura.

Pt presents w/ chronic, non-progressive chorea starting in early childhood, persistent throughout life. Fam hx pos for similar involuntary dance-like movements across 3 gens, consistent w/ benign hereditary chorea. Neg for recent meds or stroke/hemichorea symptoms. Vitals: BP 120/80, HR 72, temp 98.6. Plan: Continue monitoring, genetic testing for NKX2-1 mutations to confirm diagnosis.

Patient: पिछले तीन हफ्तों से मुझे चक्कर आ रहे हैं और कानों में भारीपन महसूस हो रहा है। मेरी सुनने की शक्ति भी अचानक कम हो गई है। Doctor: S: 45 वर्षीय महिला मरीज, पिछले 21 दिनों से आवर्तक चक्कर (episodic vertigo) की शिकायत लेकर आई हैं। साथ ही दोनों कानों में 'सेंसरीन्यूरल हियरिंग लॉस' का अनुभव हो रहा है। कान में सीटी बजने (tinnitus) की शिकायत है, लेकिन कान का कोई पिछला इतिहास नहीं है। O: बीपी 130/85 mmHg, पल्स 78 bpm। कान की जांच में पर्दा सामान्य है। ऑडियोमेट्री में द्विपक्षीय प्रगतिशील सुनने की हानि (progressive bilateral SNHL) दिखी। डिक्स-हॉलपाइक परीक्षण नकारात्मक है, जो BPPV की संभावना को खारिज करता है। न तो सिरदर्द का इतिहास है (माइग्रेन नहीं) और न ही 'फ्लक्चुएटिंग' लक्षण (मेनियर नहीं)। A: ऑटोइम्यून इनर ईयर डिजीज (AIED)। यह तेजी से बढ़ती सुनने की हानि और द्विपक्षीय वेस्टिबुलर लक्षणों के आधार पर है। P: स्टेरायडल उपचार शुरू किया गया है। बेसलाइन रक्त परीक्षण और ऑटोइम्यून प्रोफाइल (ANA, RF) के लिए भेजा गया है। ईएनटी विशेषज्ञ के साथ फॉलो-अप निर्धारित है।

72M pt c/o exertional angina. PMH: CABG 10y ago w/ synthetic graft. Vitals: BP 135/85, HR 72, O2 98%. Exam: regular rhythm, no edema. Stress test suggestive of ischemia. Cath revealed focal stenosis in prosthetic bypass conduit; native vessels and vein grafts patent. Rx: ASA, statin, cardiology follow-up for intervention.

Patient: Mal de gorge et nez qui coule depuis 2 jours. Doctor: T 38.2, gorge rouge, pas d'exsudat, poumons clairs. Diagnostic: rhinopharyngite aiguë. Plan: paracétamol PRN, repos, hydratation. Revoir si pas d'amélioration après 5 jours.

Pt: 45yo M, hx of hypothyroidism, presents with c/o persistent sensation of a 'full mouth'. Reports difficulty with enunciation and frequent tongue biting over the past six months. Denies pain, burning, or recent trauma. No history of allergic reactions. Denies smoking or EtOH. Vitals: BP 132/84, HR 78, Temp 98.6F, O2 sat 99%. Exam: Oral cavity reveals a globally enlarged, symmetric tongue that extends beyond the dental arches during speech. No signs of erythema, ulceration, or denudation of papillae noted. Tongue surface appears uniform, moist, and lacks the characteristic scalloping or map-like migratory patches seen in superficial mucosal disorders. No signs of fissuring. Imp: Macroglossia. The significant proportional increase in tongue muscle bulk without signs of papillary atrophy or localized inflammation confirms the enlargement is deep-seated rather than mucosal. Plan: 1. Referral to ENT and Endocrinology to rule out underlying systemic endocrine or infiltrative processes. 2. Sleep study to evaluate for obstructive sleep apnea secondary to mass effect. 3. Avoidance of oral trauma; follow-up in 4 weeks.

Subjective: A 54-year-old female presents with complaints of persistent, diffuse thickening of the skin on the soles of both feet and palms of her hands. Patient notes the issue has been worsening over the last few years, making it uncomfortable to walk. She denies any recent trauma, fungal infections, or chemical exposures. Family history is non-contributory. Objective: Vitals: BP 122/78, HR 72, Temp 98.6F. Exam reveals hyperkeratotic, yellowish plaques involving the entire plantar surfaces and palmar aspects of the digits. No erythema, fissuring, or secondary infection noted. Nails are unremarkable. Assessment: Diffuse thickening of the skin of the palms and soles consistent with non-syndromic palmoplantar keratoderma. Plan: 1. Prescribe high-potency topical urea cream (40%) to apply nightly under occlusion to soften plaques. 2. Recommend daily mechanical debridement using a pumice stone after bathing. 3. Advise moisturizing with thick emollients throughout the day. 4. Follow up in three months to monitor for response and assess for potential hyperhidrosis or need for systemic retinoid therapy if topical management fails.

Pt presents w/ chronic neck pain, worse w/ rotation. Exam shows limited ROM, no radiculopathy or focal neuro deficits. Imaging confirms C5-C6 disc space narrowing w/ prominent osteophyte formation at the vertebral endplate. No evidence of herniation or cord compression noted. Will start PT and NSAIDs for symptomatic relief.

Doctor: Buenos días, pase adelante. Cuénteme qué lo trae hoy por la consulta. Patient: Doctor, desde hace tres días siento un ardor muy molesto al orinar y me sale una secreción clara por el pene. No he tenido fiebre, pero la incomodidad es constante. Doctor: Entiendo, es bastante molesto. Vamos a revisar sus signos vitales: su presión es 120/80, frecuencia cardíaca 72 y temperatura 36.6 grados. Al examen físico no observo masas, induraciones ni signos de colecciones purulentas que sugieran un absceso. No hay lesiones herpéticas ni hallazgos de otras infecciones específicas en los labios uretrales. Patient: ¿Qué cree que tengo? Estoy preocupado. Doctor: Basado en sus síntomas de disuria y secreción, pero sin evidencia de complicaciones como abscesos o infecciones bacterianas específicas identificadas hasta ahora, su diagnóstico es una uretritis no específica. Es una inflamación del conducto urinario que no se debe a un patógeno único o complicado. Patient: ¿Y eso cómo se trata? Doctor: Vamos a empezar con un ciclo de antibióticos de amplio espectro para cubrir la inflamación y le pido por favor abstenerse de actividad sexual hasta terminar el tratamiento. Si no mejora en una semana, haremos más pruebas.

Pt: 28F, healthy, presents with concerns regarding persistent lack of sexual interest. Hx: Pt reports she has never experienced sexual desire in her life. However, she notes that this absence of desire is strictly limited to her current long-term partner of 3 years. When asked about other potential partners or past crushes, she describes feeling normal libido levels, confirming this is a situational response to her current relationship dynamic. No history of sexual trauma or hormonal imbalances. Ex: Vitals stable. Pmh: Unremarkable. Exam: Vagina healthy, no signs of atrophy or inflammation. Pelvic floor tone WNL. Imp: Hypoactive sexual desire dysfunction, lifelong, situational. Unlike generalized forms, her libido is intact in other contexts, indicating a specific relational trigger rather than a systemic or neurobiological baseline deficit. Plan: Referral to couples therapy to address interpersonal conflict and relational dynamics. Discussed communication exercises and scheduling intimate time. Follow up in 6 weeks to evaluate if shift in relational satisfaction impacts her subjective desire levels. Education provided on arousal non-concordance.

Pt: 28yo G2P1, 39wks gestation. Presents in active labor with prolonged second stage. Hx: Unremarkable prenatal course. Exam: Vitals stable, BP 120/78, P 88. Sterile vaginal exam reveals amniotic membranes ruptured with clear fluid. Cervix fully dilated. Palpation of the presenting part reveals a transverse lie with the fetal scapula felt at the internal os. No head, feet, or face palpable. Imp: Obstructed labor secondary to shoulder presentation. The fetus is positioned horizontally, preventing engagement and descent into the birth canal. This is distinct from breech or cephalic malpresentations as the long axis of the fetus is perpendicular to the maternal spine. Plan: Unable to deliver vaginally. Discussed risks/benefits with pt. Proceeding to urgent low-transverse Cesarean section. Anesthesia notified. Neonatology team briefed for potential respiratory distress. Consent obtained.

Pt: Mtoto ana cataracts, viziwi, na PDA. Mama alikuwa na upele mwilini mimba changa. Doctor: Mtoto ana dalili za kawaida za Rubella ya kuzaliwa. Vitals: Stable. Plan: Echo, audiometry, na ufuatiliaji wa maendeleo ya mtoto. Hali inathibitisha maambukizi ya Rubella wakati wa ujauzito.

Doctor: أهلاً بك يا سيدة فاطمة. كيف حال الطفل أحمد اليوم؟ Patient: أهلاً دكتور، لاحظت وجود فتحة مجرى البول في مكان غير طبيعي في الأسفل عند منطقة الحشفة. Doctor: دعيني أفحصه. نعم، الفتحة تقع تحديداً عند منطقة التاج، وهي الحافة التي تفصل بين رأس القضيب وجسمه، وليست في نهاية الرأس. هذا ما نسميه إحليل تحتي تاجي. Patient: هل هذا النوع يحتاج إلى جراحة؟ وهل يختلف عن الأنواع الأخرى؟ Doctor: نعم، كونه يقع في منطقة التاج تحديداً يصنفه كإحليل تحتي تاجي، وهو يختلف عن الأنواع التي تقع في رأس الحشفة أو في أجزاء أخرى من جسم القضيب. العلامات الحيوية للطفل مستقرة والنمو طبيعي. سأقوم بإحالة أحمد إلى جراح المسالك البولية للأطفال لتقييم الحاجة للإصلاح الجراحي لتصحيح مسار الفتحة وتجميل المنطقة. Patient: شكراً جزيلاً يا دكتور، سأقوم بحجز الموعد فوراً. Doctor: العفو، سأكتب تقريراً مفصلاً للجراح موضحاً موقع الفتحة التاجي بدقة.

Doctor: नमस्ते, आप कैसी महसूस कर रही हैं? प्रसव के बाद छह हफ्ते हो गए हैं, क्या सब ठीक चल रहा है? Patient: डॉक्टर साहब, प्रसव के बाद से ही मुझे बहुत थकान रहती है और पेट के निचले हिस्से में अजीब सा भारीपन और दर्द महसूस होता है। कभी-कभी बहुत ज्यादा घबराहट और चिड़चिड़ापन भी होता है। Doctor: ठीक है, मैं आपकी जांच करता हूँ। बीपी 120/80 है, पल्स 82 है। पेट के परीक्षण में गर्भाशय अभी भी थोड़ा कोमल लग रहा है और आपको हल्का दर्द है। प्रसव के बाद शरीर को रिकवर होने में समय लगता है और आपके ये लक्षण प्रसवोत्तर स्थिति या प्रसव के बाद की तकलीफों के दायरे में आते हैं। यह अक्सर होता है, लेकिन हमें इसे नजरअंदाज नहीं करना चाहिए। Patient: क्या यह ठीक हो जाएगा? मुझे बहुत चिंता होती है। Doctor: घबराइए नहीं, यह प्रसव के बाद की सामान्य शारीरिक और मानसिक परेशानी है। मैं आपको कुछ विटामिन और दर्द के लिए दवा दे रहा हूँ। साथ ही, पर्याप्त आराम करें और पौष्टिक आहार लें। अगर दर्द बढ़े या तेज बुखार आए, तो तुरंत वापस आएं। हम अगले हफ्ते फिर से फॉलो-अप करेंगे।

Paciente: Homem, 45 anos, relata dor aguda em região de hemitórax direito após esforço físico ao levantar caixa pesada no trabalho ontem. Nega dispneia, febre ou perda de consciência. Sinais vitais: PA 130/80 mmHg, FC 88 bpm, FR 16 irpm, SatO2 98%. Exame físico: Paciente relata dor à palpação local em musculatura intercostal direita. Sem deformidades, crepitações ou enfisema subcutâneo. Ausculta pulmonar limpa e simétrica. Impressão: Lesão traumática de musculatura torácica. Plano: Analgesia com dipirona 1g de 6/6h e anti-inflamatório tópico. Solicito repouso relativo de atividades de carga por 7 dias. Retorno em caso de piora da dor ou surgimento de dispneia. Doctor: Alguma melhora com a medicação? Patient: Sinto que incomoda menos ao respirar fundo, doutor, mas ainda dói ao me mexer.

Paciente: Joao Silva, 42 anos. Hx: Paciente relata cefaleia recorrente e fadiga. Nega uso de substancias. Relata que vive ha 6 meses em uma garagem sem janelas, com forte cheiro de mofo, sem saneamento basico adequado ou ventilacao, o que tem agravado sua rinite e mal-estar geral. Nao e desabrigado, pois possui contrato de locacao, mas a moradia e insalubre. Ex: PA 130/85, FC 78, FR 18, Tax 36.5C. Exame fisico demonstra mucosas hiperemicas e presenca de bolor nas roupas do paciente. Imp: Condicoes de habitacao inadequadas. O quadro clinico atual e decorrente diretamente da precariedade estrutural da moradia, nao configurando situacao de rua. Plan: Orientacao sobre limpeza do ambiente e necessidade de busca por habitacao com condicoes sanitarias minimas. Encaminhamento para assistencia social para auxilio na transicao para uma moradia salubre. Doctor: Preciso que voce tente encontrar um local mais ventilado, pois esse mofo esta afetando sua respiracao. Patient: Eu sei, doutor, mas e o que consigo pagar agora, mesmo sendo um lugar tao ruim.

Pt presents w/ fever, malaise, & non-blanching petechial rash. VS: T 103.2, P 118, BP 105/65, O2 96%. Exam: Nuchal rigidity negative, but toxic appearance. Labs pending. Clinical suspicion for invasive N. meningitidis infection. Start ceftriaxone IV immediately and notify public health. Plan: Admit to ICU for close monitoring of systemic status.

Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gable. I have reviewed the pathology results from your recent excisional biopsy. The tissue analysis shows clear evidence of pleomorphic lobular carcinoma in situ. Patient: Is that the same thing as regular LCIS? Doctor: Not exactly. While it is related to standard LCIS, the pleomorphic variety features cells that look more aggressive under the microscope. We see significant nuclear enlargement and higher grade features compared to classic lobular disease, though it remains non-invasive. We specifically ruled out ductal involvement, so it is strictly a lobular process. Vitals today show a BP of 128/82, heart rate 72, and BMI 26. Physical exam confirms the incision site is healing well with no signs of nipple changes or discharge associated with Paget disease. Patient: So what is the next step? Doctor: Because this subtype behaves more like ductal carcinoma in situ regarding risk, we need to be aggressive. Plan: I am referring you to oncology to discuss adjuvant hormonal therapy to reduce your risk of progression, and we will schedule more frequent high-risk breast screenings moving forward.

Pt: 42yo F presents with acute fatigue and DOE over past 2 weeks. Pt reports recent viral URI. No prior anemia history. Hx: Negative for thymoma, autoimmune disease, or exposure to parvovirus B19 in household. Ex: Vitals: BP 118/76, HR 92, Temp 37.0C, O2 sat 98% RA. Exam: Pale conjunctiva, no HSM or LAD. Labs: Hgb 6.2 g/dL, MCV 94 fL, Reticulocyte count 0.1%, WBC 5.2, Plt 210k. Peripheral smear shows normocytic normochromic RBCs. Bone marrow bx demonstrates severe depletion of erythroid precursors with preserved myeloid and megakaryocytic lineages. Parvovirus PCR positive. Imp: Acute acquired pure red cell aplasia secondary to acute parvovirus B19 infection. Plan: Pt admitted for PRBC transfusion. IVIG 1g/kg daily for 2 days initiated. Serial reticulocyte counts to monitor for recovery. Hematology consult for ongoing management and potential immunosuppression if persistent.

Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gable. What brings you in? Patient: About an hour after I ate some shrimp salad at lunch, my face started swelling up and I got these huge, itchy red welts all over my arms and chest. Doctor: Any stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting? Patient: No, just the swelling and the itching. My lips feel very puffy. Doctor: Looking at your vitals, your blood pressure is 118/76 and heart rate is 82. Your lungs sound clear. Those raised, red wheals are classic hives, and the swelling in your lips is angioedema. Because these appeared shortly after consuming shellfish and are strictly skin-related, this is food-induced urticaria. It is a specific immune reaction to the shrimp, not a gut issue or a skin contact rash. I am going to prescribe an oral antihistamine and we need to avoid all shellfish moving forward. We will keep you here for another thirty minutes to ensure the swelling doesn't progress before you head home. Patient: Thank you, Doctor. I feel a bit better already.

المريض: طفل عمره 8 سنوات حضر مع والديه. التاريخ المرضي: يعاني من فقدان سمع توصيلي وحسي عصبي ثنائي الجانب منذ الولادة، مع تضخم ملحوظ في الغدة الدرقية. نتائج الفحص: الضغط 105/65، النبض 85، الحرارة 37. غدة درقية متضخمة وغير مؤلمة، لا توجد علامات قصور درقي حاد حالياً. الملاحظات: أظهر اختبار بيركلورات البوتاسيوم وجود خلل في العضوية اليودية. التشخيص: متلازمة بيندريد. الخطة: طلب اختبار جيني لطفرات جين SLC26A4، البدء بجرعة تعويضية من ليفوثيروكسين، متابعة دورية مع أخصائي الأنف والأذن والحنجرة لمراقبة السمع، وتوجيه العائلة للاستشارة الوراثية. Patient: أنا قلق بشأن تأخر نموه وتضخم رقبته. Doctor: هذا مرتبط بخلل في استقلاب اليود في الغدة الدرقية مع مشكلة السمع، وسنبدأ الخطة العلاجية فوراً.

Hx: Mgonjwa wa kiume mwenye umri wa miaka 34, ana historia ya Bipolar type I. Anaripoti hali ya huzuni kubwa kwa wiki tatu zilizopita, kukosa usingizi, na uchovu. Hakuna mawazo ya kujidhuru. Ana historia ya kipindi cha mania miezi sita iliyopita. Ex: Vitals: BP 120/80, HR 72, Temp 36.6. Mgonjwa anaonekana mwenye huzuni, kuzungumza polepole, mawazo yamepungua kasi. Hakuna dalili za saikolojia (hallucinations/delusions). Imp: Ugonjwa wa Bipolar aina ya kwanza, kipindi cha sasa cha huzuni ya wastani bila dalili za saikolojia. Plan: Doctor: 'Je, unakula vizuri?' Patient: 'Sina hamu ya kula, daktari.' Doctor: 'Tutaongeza dozi ya mood stabilizer na kuanza ushauri nasaha.' Fuatilia baada ya wiki mbili.

Patient is a 42-year-old female presenting with 3 days of progressive lower extremity weakness and sensory level at T10. She reports urinary urgency and mid-back pain. Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 78, T 99.1F, SpO2 98%. Exam reveals 3/5 strength in bilateral quadriceps and hamstrings, hyperreflexia in the lower extremities, and positive Babinski sign bilaterally. Pinprick sensation is diminished below the umbilicus. Labs show mild leukocytosis. MRI of the thoracic spine demonstrates hyperintense signal within the central cord extending over three vertebral segments, consistent with transverse inflammatory pathology. No compression or disc herniation seen. Assessment: Acute transverse myelitis. Plan: Admit for high-dose IV methylprednisolone pulse therapy. Obtain CSF studies including oligoclonal bands and NMO/MOG antibodies to rule out secondary causes. Neurology consult requested for further workup and to discuss potential plasmapheresis if refractory to steroids. Physical therapy to initiate mobility training pending stabilization.

Subjective: A 4-year-old male presents for a routine vision screening. Parents report the child frequently bumps into objects and tilts his head while watching television. No history of ocular trauma or systemic disease. Objective: Vitals: BP 98/62, HR 92, RR 18. Physical exam reveals a cooperative toddler. Slit-lamp examination shows bilateral clouding of the crystalline lenses. Fundus exam is difficult to visualize due to significant opacification, but no obvious retinal pathology is noted. Intraocular pressures are within normal limits OU. Assessment: Bilateral infantile cataract, etiology currently unspecified. The findings are consistent with lens opacities that interfere with normal visual development. Plan: Referral to pediatric ophthalmology for surgical evaluation and potential lensectomy. We will discuss the risks and benefits of surgery versus observation with the parents. Baseline workup including TORCH titers and metabolic screening ordered to rule out underlying causes. Patient will return for follow-up after specialist evaluation.

Doctor: Hujambo, nini kinakusumbua leo? Patient: Daktari, nahisi kizunguzungu kikali kinachokuja na kuondoka. Kinaanza ghafla, nahisi kama chumba kinazunguka, na wakati mwingine natapika. Doctor: Hiki kizunguzungu kinadumu kwa muda gani? Patient: Mara nyingi kinadumu kama dakika ishirini hadi saa moja, kisha kinatulia kidogo. Vitals: BP 130/85, Pulse 78, Temp 36.7. Doctor: Baada ya kukuchunguza na kuangalia masikio yako na usawa wa mwili, naona una tatizo la mfumo wa usawa linalojitokeza mara kwa mara, tunaliita episodic vestibular syndrome. Bado hatujajua chanzo kamili kinachosababisha hivi vipindi vya kuzunguka kichwa, kwani dalili zako hazionyeshi ugonjwa mmoja maalum kama Meniere au shida zingine za ndani ya sikio. Patient: Sawa daktari, nifanye nini? Doctor: Nitakupatia dawa za kutuliza kichefuchefu na kizunguzungu kwa sasa. Tunahitaji kufanya vipimo zaidi vya kusikia na picha za ubongo ili kuona kama kuna sababu nyingine za ndani. Tafadhali pumzika unapohisi dalili na uepuke kuendesha gari wakati huu. Tutafuatilia hali yako baada ya wiki mbili.

Doctor: Good morning, Mr. Henderson. I have reviewed your follow-up echocardiogram from yesterday, which was three weeks after your heart attack. Patient: Thanks, Doc. I have been feeling okay, just a little tired. Any concerns? Doctor: The imaging shows that your heart rhythm is steady and your valves are functioning well. However, there is a stationary blood clot attached to the inner wall of the left ventricle where the muscle was damaged during your infarct. This is a mural thrombus. Patient: Is that going to cause a rupture or heart failure? Doctor: It is not a rupture, aneurysm, or a septal defect. Your heart wall structure is stable. My main concern is that if a piece of this clot breaks off, it could travel elsewhere. Vitals today show a BP of 128/82, heart rate 72, and O2 saturation 98%. We need to start you on long-term anticoagulation therapy immediately to dissolve this mass and prevent it from throwing a clot. Patient: Okay, I understand the plan. How long will I be on the medication? Doctor: We will start now and re-evaluate with another ultrasound in six weeks. We want to be aggressive because this complication is a direct result of the recent myocardial injury.

Doctor: Good morning, Mr. Henderson. I have reviewed your high-resolution CT scan. We are looking at progressive scarring in the lung bases without any signs of inflammation or emphysema. Patient: I have just been so winded lately, even walking to the mailbox. Is this reversible? Doctor: Unfortunately, the scarring we see, known as honeycombing, is permanent. Based on the pattern and the fact that you have no history of smoking or autoimmune disease, this is idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. This is a chronic condition where the lung tissue thickens for unknown reasons. Vitals: BP 135/85, HR 78, O2 sat 91% on room air. Exam: bibasilar inspiratory crackles present. Plan: We will start you on antifibrotic therapy to slow the progression. I am also referring you to pulmonary rehab and supplemental oxygen for exertion. We need to monitor your lung function closely with spirometry every three months to track the decline. It is crucial we keep you current on your pneumonia and flu vaccinations.

Doctor: नमस्ते, बताइए आज क्या समस्या हो रही है? Patient: डॉक्टर साहब, पिछले कुछ दिनों से पेट के ऊपरी हिस्से में बहुत जलन और दर्द हो रहा है। कभी-कभी लगता है जैसे पेट में छिल गया हो। Doctor: क्या आपको कोई दवा लेने की आदत है या हाल ही में कोई संक्रमण हुआ है? Patient: नहीं, मैं कोई दर्द निवारक दवा नहीं लेता और न ही मुझे कोई बुखार या संक्रमण है। Doctor: ठीक है, देखते हैं। (जांच के बाद) आपका बीपी 120/80 है और पेट दबाने पर हल्का दर्द महसूस हो रहा है। एंडोस्कोपी रिपोर्ट से स्पष्ट है कि आपके पेट की अंदरूनी परत में ऊपरी सतह पर कुछ घाव या घिसाब (erosion) हैं। इसमें कोई बैक्टीरिया या दवा का असर नहीं दिख रहा है। यह पेट की अंदरूनी झिल्ली का सतही घिसाब है। Patient: तो इसका मतलब क्या है, क्या यह गंभीर है? Doctor: नहीं, यह चिंता की बात नहीं है। यह पेट की म्यूकोसा में मामूली कटाव है। मैं आपको एंटासिड दवाएं लिख रहा हूँ और खाने में परहेज रखना होगा। अगले दो हफ्ते तक मिर्च-मसाले वाली चीजें न खाएं। यह अपने आप ठीक हो जाएगा। Patient: शुक्रिया डॉक्टर, मैं आपकी सलाह का पालन करूँगा।

Pt presents w/ persistent erythematous indurated plaques on trunk. Biopsy shows non-specific histiocytic and granulomatous infiltrate, dermis. No systemic involvement noted on labs or exam. Suspect cutaneous histiocytic-granulomatous process. Plan: refer to derm for further IHC staining and potential excisional bx to clarify etiology. Monitor for new lesions.

Pt: 62 y/o female marathon runner presents with localized mid-thoracic back pain, 6/10 intensity, worsening over 6 weeks despite rest. Denies acute trauma, falls, or sudden lifting incidents. Pain is focal, exacerbated by running and spinal flexion. Vitals: BP 122/78, HR 72, temp 98.6F. Exam: No neurovascular deficits. Tenderness to palpation at T7 spinous process; ROM limited by discomfort. No evidence of ankylosis or osteophyte bridging on palpation. MRI reveals T7 vertebral body superior endplate hairline stress reaction with surrounding marrow edema, consistent with repetitive microtrauma rather than sudden compressive collapse or inflammatory fusion. No posterior element hypertrophy or kissing spines noted. Assessment: T7 fatigue fracture of vertebra, likely secondary to repetitive loading. Plan: Transition to low-impact activity, core strengthening physical therapy, and DXA scan to evaluate bone density status. Avoid high-impact loading for 8-12 weeks. Follow up in 6 weeks for repeat imaging to ensure appropriate callous formation.

Doctor: المريض يشتكي من ألم خاصر مزمن، فحص الـ CT أظهر حصوة كبيرة تشغل حويضة الكلية وكؤوسها بشكل قرن الأيل. Patient: أشعر بضغط مستمر في جنبي. Plan: تقرر إجراء جراحة تفتيت الحصى عبر الجلد PCNL لضمان إزالة حصوة قرن الأيل الممتدة. المريض مستقر حيوياً والضغط 120/80 والنبض 75.

Pt, 45F, reports total inability to achieve climax during masturbation or intercourse for past 6mo. Prev normal sexual function until recent onset. PE/labs wnl. Dx: Acquired generalized anorgasmia. Pt clear this is not context-specific and a new change from baseline. R/o depression/med SE. Plan: Pelvic floor PT referral, counseling, follow up 4wks.

Hx: ታካሚዋ በቅርቡ ውጭ ሀገር ፅንስ ማስወረድ አድርጋ አሁን ለሦስት ቀናት የሚቆይ የማህፀን ህመም እና ትኩሳት ቅሬታ ይዛ ቀረበች። Patient: "ከሆዴ በታች በጣም ያመኛል፤ ትኩሳትም አለብኝ።" Ex: Vitals: BP 110/70, HR 98, Temp 38.5C. መመርመርያ፡ ማህፀኗ በምርመራ ሲነካ ህመም አለው፣ ከማህፀን በር የሚወጣ መግል መሰል ፈሳሽ ታይቷል። በአልትራሳውንድ ምርመራ የማህፀን ውስጠኛው ክፍል ሙሉ በሙሉ ባዶ ሆኖ ተገኝቷል፣ ምንም የተረፈ ቲሹ የለም። Imp: ፅንስ ማስወረድ የተጠናቀቀ ቢሆንም፣ በዳሌ አካባቢ የባክቴሪያ ኢንፌክሽን መኖሩ ተረጋግጧል። Plan: ታካሚዋ ሆስፒታል ገብታ በደም ሥር የሚሰጡ ጠንካራ አንቲባዮቲኮችን (IV antibiotics) እንድትጀምር ታዘዘ። ክትትል ይደረጋል።

Doctor: Hujambo, nimepitia ripoti ya ultrasound yako. Je, unajisikiaje leo? Patient: Sijambo daktari, nina wasiwasi kidogo kuhusu matokeo yale. Je, kuna tatizo lolote na mtoto wangu? Doctor: Mtoto anaendelea vizuri kwa ujumla, lakini nimeona kitu kwenye vipimo kuhusu urefu wa kamba ya kitovu. Hii inamaanisha kuwa kamba ya kitovu ina urefu ambao hauko ndani ya kiwango cha kawaida, inaweza kuwa ndefu sana au fupi sana, lakini hatuwezi kusema hasa ni kipi kwa sasa. Hali hii inaitwa hitilafu ya urefu wa kamba ya kitovu. Vitals: Shinikizo la damu 120/80, mapigo ya moyo 82, uzito kilo 65. Findings: Uchunguzi wa ultrasound unaonyesha kamba ya kitovu ina urefu usio wa kawaida, jambo ambalo linaweza kuathiri mtoto wakati wa ukuaji au kujifungua. Plan: Tutafuatilia ukuaji wa mtoto kwa karibu zaidi kupitia vipimo vya mara kwa mara vya ultrasound. Pia, utafanyiwa vipimo vya kufuatilia mapigo ya moyo ya mtoto mara kwa mara ili kuhakikisha usalama wake hadi wakati wa kujifungua. Tafadhali njoo ofisini kwangu baada ya wiki mbili kwa ukaguzi mwingine.

Doctor: Good morning, Sarah. I’ve reviewed the imaging of your newborn's upper extremities. Everything from the shoulder down through the elbow, forearm, and wrist is perfectly formed and present. However, the x-rays confirm that the hand itself is missing all five fingers and the underlying metacarpal bones. Patient: So, the arm is there, but just the fingers didn't grow? Doctor: Exactly. We call this adactyly. It is specifically a deficiency where the digits are absent, but the rest of the hand anatomy, including the carpal bones and the wrist structure, is preserved. Because the humerus, radius, and ulna are all normal and the wrist exists, this distinguishes it from other limb reductions like acheiria or radial deficiencies. Vitals: HR 135, RR 42, Temp 98.6 F. Findings: Bilateral presence of proximal and distal arm segments; complete lack of phalanges and metacarpals on the right side. Plan: Refer to pediatric orthotics and prosthetics for early developmental assessment. Schedule follow-up with genetic counseling to discuss potential causes. We will prioritize physical therapy to encourage full range of motion at the wrist and elbow joints.

Doctor: مريض ٤٥ سنة، يعاني من ألم حاد ومفاجئ بالجسم، لا توجد إصابة واضحة أو تاريخ جراحي، العلامات الحيوية: الضغط ١٢٥/٨٠، النبض ٨٢. Patient: أشعر بألم شديد لا أستطيع تحديده، يؤلمني كل مكان. Plan: وصف مسكنات ألم، متابعة الحالة خلال ٤٨ ساعة، إرشاد المريض للراحة.

Doctor: Bonjour Madame, que vous est-il arrivé ? Patient: Je faisais du jardinage, j'ai glissé et je me suis empalée le côté du cou sur une branche fine et pointue qui dépassait. Je l'ai retirée tout de suite, il n'y a rien dedans. Doctor: Voyons cela. Le saignement a bien diminué. Je vois un orifice punctiforme isolé sur le muscle sterno-cléido-mastoïdien, profond mais étroit, typique d'une plaie par perforation, sans aucun débris à l'intérieur. Pas de lacération, pas de morsure, juste ce point d'entrée net. Les signes vitaux sont stables : tension 125/80, pouls 72. Je vais nettoyer la zone, appliquer un pansement stérile et vérifier votre rappel antitétanique. C'est une plaie pénétrante simple sans corps étranger. Il faudra surveiller l'apparition de rougeur ou de fièvre dans les prochains jours. Patient: Très bien, je comprends, merci docteur.

Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gable. It is that time of year again. Are you here for your annual seasonal flu shot? Patient: Yes, I am. I try to stay on top of it so I do not end up bedridden with the chills and body aches like I was a few years ago. Doctor: That is a smart move, especially given your history of mild asthma. The current circulating strains are quite active, and we want to ensure you have coverage for the anticipated influenza season. Vitals today show a blood pressure of 128/76, heart rate 72, and temperature 98.6 F. Your lungs sound clear bilaterally. Patient: Great. My husband already got his at the pharmacy, but I prefer coming in here. Doctor: I am happy to provide that for you. Given that you are up to date on your other series like shingles and pneumonia, today we will just focus on the seasonal influenza vaccine. I will have the nurse bring that in shortly. You should be set for the next twelve months. Do you have any questions before we proceed? Patient: No, just keep the needle steady!

Patient is a 54-year-old male presenting with progressive dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and intermittent low-grade fevers. He reports night sweats over the past month. Vitals: T 99.2F, BP 105/65, HR 92, RR 18, SpO2 94% on RA. Physical exam reveals jugular venous distension and distant heart sounds. There is no peripheral lymphadenopathy, no skin lesions, and no abdominal tenderness or joint swelling. Chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly with a globular silhouette. Echo demonstrates a significant pericardial effusion with fibrinous debris. Pericardiocentesis was performed; cytology negative for malignancy, but PCR and AFB culture of the fluid are positive for M. tuberculosis. Impression: Tuberculous pericarditis and myocardial involvement. Plan: Start RIPE therapy (Rifampin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, Ethambutol). Monitor for signs of cardiac tamponade. Follow up with cardiology for repeat echocardiography in two weeks. Consult infectious disease for long-term TB management and contact tracing.

Doctor: Good morning, Mr. Henderson. I have reviewed the results from your recent upper endoscopy and the tissue biopsies. Patient: Thanks, Doctor. I have been really worried about this persistent trouble swallowing. Doctor: I understand. The pathology report confirms that you have a malignant tumor known as adenocarcinoma of the esophagus. This is a type of glandular cancer that has developed in the lining of your food pipe. Vitals today show a blood pressure of 132/84, pulse 76, and your weight is down five pounds since last visit. Physical exam reveals some mild tenderness in the upper abdomen, but otherwise clear lung sounds. Patient: What are the next steps? Doctor: We need to stage this properly to see how far it has spread. I am ordering a PET-CT scan today and I will refer you to an oncology surgeon to discuss our treatment strategy, which will likely involve a combination of therapies. We want to get you feeling better and address the swallowing issues as soon as possible. I will have my staff coordinate these appointments before you leave the clinic today.

Pt presents w/ Hct 62% and Hgb 21. Pt admits to repetitive 'blood doping' via autologous RBC re-infusion over past 3 mos to improve athletic endurance. Vitals: BP 145/92, HR 72. Exam reveals facial plethora. Plan: Discontinue re-infusions, therapeutic phlebotomy 500mL weekly, and monitor CBC closely.

Doctor: Bonjour Madame, je vois ici que vous avez eu des infections sinuso-pulmonaires à répétition ces derniers mois. Comment vous sentez-vous aujourd'hui ? Patient: Je suis toujours épuisée, docteur. J'ai eu trois épisodes de sinusite et deux bronchites depuis l'automne. C'est très frustrant. Doctor: Je comprends. J'ai reçu les résultats de vos examens immunologiques. Ils montrent quelque chose de spécifique : vos taux d'IgG et d'IgA sont très bas, mais vos taux d'IgM sont tout à fait normaux, voire légèrement élevés. De plus, vos analyses montrent que votre nombre de lymphocytes B est tout à fait dans la norme. Patient: Qu'est-ce que cela signifie concrètement ? Doctor: Il s'agit d'un déficit immunitaire humoral sélectif. Vos cellules B sont présentes, mais elles ne produisent pas assez d'anticorps protecteurs comme les IgG ou les IgA. Nous allons devoir commencer des perfusions régulières d'immunoglobulines pour compenser ce manque et prévenir ces infections. Vitals: TA 120/80 mmHg, pouls 72 bpm, température 37°C. Findings: Examen pulmonaire clair, pas de foyers infectieux actifs ce jour. Plan: Initiation de la thérapie de substitution par immunoglobulines intraveineuses et suivi mensuel du taux d'IgG résiduel.

Pt, 45F, c/o neck fullness & fatigue. Vitals: BP 120/80, HR 78, BMI 26. PE: thyroid palpable, firm, non-tender, no discrete nodules. Labs: TSH elevated, FT4 low-nl. Thyroid US showing generalized enlargement without focal masses. Consider endemic iodine deficiency state. Plan: order 24h urinary iodine level, start levothyroxine, recheck in 6w.

Doctor: नमस्ते। आज आप क्यों आए हैं? Patient: डॉक्टर साहब, मेरा 10 साल का बेटा स्कूल में बहुत संघर्ष कर रहा है। उसे चीजें समझने में काफी समय लगता है और वो रोजमर्रा के काम जैसे पैसे गिनना या समय देखना ठीक से नहीं कर पा रहा है। डॉक्टर: ठीक है। (परीक्षण और रिपोर्ट की समीक्षा के बाद) इसके शारीरिक माप सामान्य हैं। मैंने उसके पिछले स्कूल के रिकॉर्ड देखे हैं। उसका व्यवहार सामाजिक रूप से काफी अच्छा है, वह अपने कपड़े खुद पहन सकता है और सरल बातचीत कर सकता है। हालांकि, उसका शैक्षणिक स्तर उसकी उम्र के अन्य बच्चों की तुलना में काफी पीछे है। वह अभी भी बुनियादी गणनाओं में अटकता है। Patient: क्या यह ठीक हो जाएगा? डॉक्टर: देखिए, मैंने इसकी स्थिति का गहराई से अध्ययन किया है। आपके बेटे को हल्की बौद्धिक विकास संबंधी समस्या है। इसका मतलब है कि उसकी सीखने की गति थोड़ी धीमी है, लेकिन वह सहायता के साथ स्वतंत्र जीवन जीना सीख सकता है। उसे मध्यम या गंभीर समस्या नहीं है, क्योंकि वह अपनी जरूरतों का ध्यान रख सकता है। हम विशेष शिक्षा और कुछ कौशल प्रशिक्षण के साथ उसे काफी मदद कर सकते हैं। Patient: समझ गया, क्या हमें कोई बड़ी चिंता करने की जरूरत है? डॉक्टर: नहीं, बस हमें धैर्य रखना होगा और उसे निरंतर सहायता प्रदान करनी होगी।

Paciente: Uso crônico de opioide para dor lombar. Doctor: Queixas de sonolência e fadiga diurna? Patient: Sim, ando dormindo mal e cansado. Exame: SatO2 92% em sono, sem obesidade ou comorbidades. Dx: Hipoventilação central induzida por uso terapêutico de opioide. Conduta: Ajuste dose fármaco e encaminhamento ao sono.

Patient: Kichwa kinauma sana na damu inatoka puani na masikioni. Doctor: BP 210/110, GCS 8. CT inaonyesha damu kwenye lobar na deep nuclei pande zote mbili, multiple sites. Plan: Admit ICU, BP control, neurosurg consult.

Hx: Paciente masculino de 42 años refiere cefaleas persistentes y cambios en su visión lateral desde hace dos meses. Doctor: ¿Nota dificultad para ver objetos a los lados? Patient: Siento que no veo a las personas que pasan por mis costados, tengo que girar mucho la cabeza. Ex: Signos vitales: PA 130/85 mmHg, FC 78 lpm. Examen neurológico destaca campimetría visual por confrontación que revela una hemianopsia bitemporal clara, con respeto de los campos visuales nasales internos y compromiso de los campos temporales externos en ambos ojos. Fondo de ojo sin edema papilar aparente. Imp: Hemianopsia bitemporal, sospechosa de lesión en el quiasma óptico por posible macroadenoma hipofisario. Plan: Solicitar RM de silla turca con contraste para descartar compresión quiasmática. Derivación urgente a oftalmología para estudio de campo visual computarizado (Humphrey) y evaluación por endocrinología para perfil hormonal completo. Seguimiento en 2 semanas con resultados de imágenes.

Doctor: Buenos días, señora. ¿Qué le trae por aquí hoy? Patient: Doctor, tengo un picor insoportable en el oído derecho desde hace una semana y siento como si tuviera escamas o piel seca saliendo de ahí. Doctor: Déjeme revisar. Veo bastante enrojecimiento en el conducto auditivo externo. Hay descamación blanquecina y grasa, típica de una dermatitis seborreica que se ha extendido al oído. Signos vitales: Presión 120/80, temperatura 36.5. Hallazgos: Inflamación de la piel del canal auditivo con descamación amarillenta y seborrea, sin secreción purulenta ni perforación del tímpano. Patient: ¿Es una infección por bacterias? Doctor: No exactamente. Lo que usted tiene es una otitis externa seborreica; es básicamente una inflamación por exceso de grasa y descamación de la piel del conducto. El plan será aplicar unas gotas con corticoide tópico por siete días para reducir la inflamación y controlar la descamación. Evite introducir bastoncillos de algodón para no irritar más la zona. ¿Tiene alguna pregunta? Patient: Entendido, doctor. Muchas gracias por la aclaración.

72yo F w/ DOE and orthopnea. PE: S4 gallop, rales at bases, 2+ pedal edema. TTE: LVEF 56%, LAE, E/e' 16, consistent w/ diastolic dysfunction. Echo confirms HFpEF. Plan: Increase furosemide, start low-dose ARNI, monitor BP/electrolytes. F/u 2wks.

Paciente: Homem, 68 anos, internado em UTI prolongada por TCE, traqueostomizado. Hx: Apresentou febre de 38.9C, secreção traqueal purulenta e piora da gasometria. Ex: FC 115 bpm, FR 28 irpm, SatO2 88%. Ausculta pulmonar com estertores crepitantes difusos em base direita. RX de tórax mostra infiltrado alveolar consolidado lobar. Imp: Pneumonia hospitalar. Cultura de aspirado traqueal confirmou crescimento de Pseudomonas aeruginosa sensível a piperacilina/tazobactam. O quadro clínico e o isolamento microbiológico confirmam pneumonia por este bacilo gram-negativo não fermentador. Doctor: Como tem sido a secreção, Sr. João? Patient: Está saindo bem verde e espessa, doutor, e sinto muita falta de ar. Doctor: Entendo, vamos ajustar seu antibiótico para cobrir esse germe que cresceu no exame e reforçar a fisioterapia respiratória. Plan: 1. Iniciar Piperacilina-Tazobactam 4,5g IV 6/6h. 2. Aumentar suporte de O2 para manter SatO2 > 92%. 3. Manter cabeceira elevada e aspiração traqueal rigorosa. 4. Nova radiografia de tórax em 48h.

Hx: Mgonjwa wa kiume mwenye umri wa miaka 45 analalamika kuhusu usaha kutoka kwenye tundu dogo karibu na njia ya haja kubwa kwa miezi mitatu. Hakuna maumivu makali wakati wa kujisaidia. Ex: Vitals: BP 120/80, HR 72, Temp 36.7. Katika uchunguzi wa rectal, nimeona tundu la nje (external opening) lenye usaha katika nafasi ya saa nne, karibu na msamba. Hakuna mipasuko mikali ya ngozi ya mfereji wa haja kubwa (kama katika fissure). Uchunguzi wa kidole unaonyesha mrija (tract) unaoenda kuelekea mfereji wa anal. Imp: Anal fistula. Plan: Nimeeleza mgonjwa kuhusu haja ya upasuaji wa kufungua mrija huu (fistulotomy). Tutaagiza vipimo vya damu na kuanza antibiotics za kuzuia maambukizi kabla ya upasuaji. Doctor: Je, unaona maumivu makali wakati wa choo? Patient: Hapana daktari, ni huo usaha tu unaonitia wasiwasi na kunichafua nguo kila siku. Doctor: Sawa, tutapanga utaratibu wa kufunga huo mrija ili kuponya tatizo hili kabisa.

Doctor: Good morning, Sarah. I see you are here today to follow up on that area on your right forearm. How has it been feeling? Patient: It is mostly just annoying, honestly. It doesn't hurt or itch anymore, but the skin is just really thick and tight where I had that deep laceration last year. It looks a bit shiny and pale compared to the rest of my arm. Doctor: Let me take a look. I see the area you are referring to. It is a well-healed, pale fibrous tissue consistent with a mature scar. There is no evidence of infection or underlying inflammation. Since the injury occurred months ago and the tissue has remodeled into a stable, non-contracting patch, this is simply a post-traumatic scar. There is no active pathology, just a residual mark from the healing process. We don't need any further intervention since it is not causing you physical impairment. Patient: Okay, that is a relief. I was worried it might be something else. Doctor: Not at all. It is just a stable skin scar. Just keep using sunscreen on it to prevent hyperpigmentation, but otherwise, it is perfectly fine.

Pt: 42M w/ hx psoriasis presents c/o chronic LBP, morning stiffness >1hr, relieved by ex. Exam: tenderness over SI joints, reduced lumbar ROM. Labs: HLA-B27+. Radiographs show bilateral sacroiliitis. Dx: Psoriatic spondyloarthritis. Plan: start adalimumab, PT referral for spinal mobility, f/u 4wks.

Doctor: እንደምን አደሩ? ዛሬ ምን ይሰማዎታል? Pt: 28yo G2P1, 26w gestation. Hx: Presents with 2-day history of localized, tender, red, rope-like cord on the medial aspect of the left calf. Denies history of varicosities prior to pregnancy. No history of DVT. S/O: Vitals stable, afebrile. Physical exam: Focal area of induration, 4cm in length, overlying a superficial saphenous vein segment. Skin is erythematous and warm to touch. No pitting edema, Homan’s sign negative. No pelvic or labial varicosities noted. Assessment: Superficial thrombophlebitis, left lower extremity, occurring during pregnancy. Clinical presentation is distinct from simple asymptomatic varicosities due to active inflammation/thrombus, and negative for deep vein involvement based on clinical exam. Plan: 1. Warm compresses to affected area BID. 2. Graduated compression stockings. 3. Encourage frequent ambulation and hydration. 4. Monitor for signs of DVT (increasing swelling or calf pain). 5. Follow up in one week if no improvement.

14d old male, umbilicus remains moist w/ sm. pink, friable mass at base post-cord sep. No signs of systemic infx, afebrile. Dx: umbilical granuloma. Plan: Silver nitrate cauterization x1 in clinic. Follow up 1wk if no improvement.

Doctor: Good morning, Marcus. Looking at your skin today, I see these multiple firm, flesh-colored bumps scattered across your face and neck, and you mentioned they have been increasing in number since puberty. Patient: Yes, they started as just a few, but now they are quite numerous and bother me. Doctor: I also noticed some small pits on your palms and noticed you have had a history of jaw cysts. Based on these features, I am diagnosing you with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. This is a genetic condition that causes hamartomas, which are benign overgrowths, to develop in your skin and other organ systems. This is distinct from other skin disorders because of the specific way these tumors form in your facial tissue, known as angiofibromas. Vitals today show a blood pressure of 122/78 and pulse of 72. Patient: Is there a way to remove the bumps? Doctor: We can discuss laser therapy for the facial lesions. Plan: I am ordering a baseline brain MRI and a renal ultrasound to monitor for any internal hamartomas. We will follow up in three months to track the progression of the skin lesions and review your imaging results.

Hx: Paciente de 62 anos, sexo feminino, relata sensacao persistente de instabilidade postural e desequilibrio ao caminhar iniciada ha 3 semanas. Nega sensacao de girar o ambiente (vertigem), desmaios ou escurecimento visual. Nega relacao com esforco fisico ou mudancas bruscas de posicao. Ex: PA 130/80 mmHg, FC 78 bpm. Otoscopia bilateral sem alteracoes. Teste de Romberg positivo com olhos fechados, indicando oscilacao lateral. Nistagmo ausente. Marcha ataxica leve, com base alargada. Imp: Transtorno do equilibrio. O quadro e distinto de vertigem ou lipotimia pela ausencia de rotacao do ambiente ou sintomas autonomicos pre-sincopais, mantendo-se como uma instabilidade persistente de base neurologica ou vestibular central. Plan: Solicito RM de encafalo para descartar lesoes estruturais e encaminhamento para fisioterapia vestibular. Recomendado evitar ambientes com tapetes soltos e usar calcados fechados para prevenir quedas. Retorno em 15 dias com exames. Doctor: Vamos investigar essa instabilidade. Patient: Doutor, sinto como se estivesse sempre pisando em algo macio, fico com medo de cair mesmo parada.

Paciente: Varón de 5 años traído por su madre tras caída con el brazo extendido. Doctor: ¿Cómo ocurrió el incidente? Paciente: Estaba jugando y al tirar de mi brazo sentí un chasquido. Hx: Dolor agudo en el codo derecho tras tracción longitudinal del antebrazo. Refiere imposibilidad para la supinación. Ex: Signos vitales estables. Se observa prominencia ósea palpable en la cara lateral del codo. No hay equimosis marcada ni deformidad grosera en la articulación humero-ulnar, descartando luxación completa de codo. Dolor exquisito sobre la cúpula radial. Rango de movimiento limitado en prono-supinación. Ligamentos colaterales estables al bostezo. Imp: Subluxación de la cabeza del radio (codo de niñera). Plan: Se realiza maniobra de reducción cerrada mediante hiperpronación del antebrazo, logrando un chasquido audible y resolución inmediata del dolor. El paciente recupera movilidad completa. Se indica observación y evitar tracciones bruscas del miembro afectado. Cita de control en 48 horas si persiste molestia.

Hx: Mgonjwa wa kiume mwenye umri wa miaka 52 anakuja na historia ya miezi minne ya kusumbuliwa na vipindi vya jasho jingi, mapigo ya moyo kwenda mbio, na kizunguzungu baada ya kufunga kula. Hana historia ya kupungua uzito au maumivu ya mgongo. Ex: Vitals: BP 120/80 mmHg, HR 72, Temp 36.7C. Palpation ya tumbo: Hakuna uvimbe unaoonekana lakini kuna unyeti kidogo epigastric. Imp: Uchunguzi wa picha za CT unaonyesha uvimbe mdogo wenye mishipa mingi kwenye mkia wa kongosho. Vipimo vya damu vinaonyesha kiwango cha juu sana cha insulini na C-peptide. Hii inashiria neoplasm ya neuroendocrine ya kongosho inayotoa insulini (insulinoma). Hii inatofautiana na adenocarcinoma ambayo mara nyingi huleta uzito kupungua na uvimbe kwenye kichwa cha kongosho. Plan: 1. Upasuaji wa kutoa uvimbe (enucleation). 2. Uchunguzi wa ziada wa homoni za damu. 3. Rufaa kwa upasuaji wa kongosho. Doctor: Tutafanya upasuaji kutoa hicho uvimbe. Patient: Sawa daktari, natumai tatizo hili la jasho litaisha.

Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gable. What brings you in today? Patient: I have just been feeling wiped out. I have had a terrible stomach bug for three days, couldn't keep water down, and now I feel dizzy every time I stand up. Doctor: I am sorry to hear that. Let's look at your vitals. Your blood pressure is 98/62 and your pulse is a bit fast at 105. Your mouth looks quite dry. Based on your symptoms of dizziness and inability to tolerate fluids, it appears you are suffering from overall volume depletion. We need to get your levels back up. Patient: That makes sense. What should we do? Doctor: I want you to start taking small, frequent sips of an electrolyte solution. If you cannot tolerate that, we will need to head to the infusion center for intravenous fluids to stabilize your status. Please avoid any heavy exertion for the next 48 hours. If you notice any confusion or stop urinating entirely, go straight to the emergency department. I will have the nurse set up a follow-up call for tomorrow morning to check on your progress.

Pt w/ adv. HF & Hx of opiate use now resolved. PSG confirms CSA w/out CSB. No alt-habits or drug use. Central events persist due to neuro-respiratory blunting from chronic renal failure. VSS: 120/80, 72, 16, 96%. Start acetazolamide; cont. CPAP for nocturnal support. Follow-up 4wks.

Doctor: Good morning, Mrs. Gable. I have reviewed your recent MRI and MRA brain scans following your persistent headaches and episodes of dizziness. Patient: I am just relieved we have an answer. Is it a tumor? Doctor: It is not a tumor. The imaging reveals an abnormal cluster of blood vessels within your brain. We call this an intracranial vascular malformation. It is essentially a tangle of vessels that has formed in a way that is not typical for your anatomy, though at this stage, the imaging does not clearly define the specific type or origin of these vessels. Vitals today show a blood pressure of 132/84 and a heart rate of 76. Neurological exam is non-focal. Patient: Does this require surgery? Doctor: Not necessarily. Because we have not classified the specific structural nature of these vessels, we will start with conservative management and referral to neurosurgery for a consultation to discuss potential monitoring versus intervention. Plan: Obtain a formal neurosurgical referral, maintain blood pressure control, and schedule a follow-up imaging study in six months to monitor for any stability changes. Avoid heavy lifting and intense strain for now.

Pt: 68 y/o F. Hx: Known uveal effusion syndrome presenting with dull ache and blurred vision in OD. Denies trauma or surgery. Ex: VA 20/40 OD. Slit lamp shows anterior rotation of the ciliary body causing shallowing of the peripheral anterior chamber but the pupil is patent and free of adhesions; no rubeosis, no epithelial or endothelial sheets, and no posterior synechiae. IOP 32 mmHg OD. Gonioscopy confirms 360-degree appositional angle closure with posterior pressure mechanism, clear iris-lens relationship excluding pupil block. Imp: Secondary angle closure glaucoma without pupillary block due to uveal effusion. Plan: Initiate topical IOP-lowering drops (latanoprost 0.005% qhs). Will schedule ultrasound biomicroscopy to confirm ciliary body position and monitor for progression. Avoid miotics. Discussed signs of acute pressure spikes with patient.

Patient: 42M, avid surfer. Hx: Complains of intermittent sense of fullness in the right ear and occasional trapped water after swimming. Denies pain, discharge, or hearing loss. Ex: Vitals stable, afebrile. Otoscopy reveals multiple, broad-based, smooth, bony protuberances arising from the medial tympanic ring of the external auditory canal bilaterally. The skin overlying these mounds is thin, pale, and intact. No signs of inflammation, debris, or wax impaction noted. The tympanic membranes are clear and mobile bilaterally. No evidence of canal narrowing or soft tissue growth. Imp: Multiple bilateral bony growths consistent with external auditory canal exostosis, likely secondary to chronic cold water exposure. These are distinct from cholesteatoma as the epithelium remains intact and non-migratory. Canal patency is well-preserved, ruling out acquired stenosis. Plan: Conservative management. Advised use of custom-fitted silicone earplugs during water activities to prevent further enlargement. Will monitor periodically for progression or potential impaction of cerumen between the bony ridges. Return to clinic if patient develops secondary otitis externa or obstructive symptoms.

Doctor: Mgonjwa ana BP 160/95 mmHg, edema miguuni, na protini kwenye mkojo +2. Hali inaashiria uharibifu wa figo kutokana na presha sugu. Patient: Nimekuwa nikihisi kuvimba miguu na kichwa kuuma sana. Plan: Kuanzisha dawa za kushusha presha na kufanya vipimo vya kreatini ya damu; kufuatilia figo kwa karibu.

Doctor: Good morning, Sarah. What brings you in today? Patient: I have had this nasty scratchy throat, a runny nose, and some sneezing for the past three days. I feel pretty run down. Doctor: Let me take a look. Your vitals show a temperature of 99.2, heart rate 78, and blood pressure 124/80. Your lungs sound clear, but your throat is a bit red without any exudate. There is no sign of involvement in your sinuses or bronchial tubes. Based on your symptoms, this is a common viral cold affecting the upper respiratory tract. It is not a deeper infection like bronchitis or a sinus issue. Patient: That is a relief. Should I take antibiotics? Doctor: No, antibiotics won't help a viral cold. We will treat this as an acute upper respiratory infection. Stick to hydration, plenty of rest, and use over-the-counter decongestants as needed for the congestion. It should resolve on its own in about a week. Let me know if you develop a high fever or difficulty breathing.

Pt: 54yo M w/ hx cirrhosis. C/o abd pain, ascites. US/Doppler shows echogenic thrombus in main portal vein w/o flow. No hepatic vein outflow obstruction. PT/INR stable. Plan: Start therapeutic anticoagulation, bridge w/ LMWH. GI follow up for endoscopy to assess variceal risk. Continue monitoring labs.

Patient: 62yo male. Hx: Presents with chronic, asymptomatic, reticulated rash on the trunk and upper thighs for several years. Denies pruritus or systemic symptoms. No history of monoclonal gammopathy. Ex: Physical exam reveals patches of mottled erythema, telangiectasia, and fine epidermal atrophy in a reticulated distribution across the chest and abdomen. No thick, scaly plaques suggestive of large plaque parapsoriasis. No indurated red-brown nodules or dermal plaques seen, making plasmacytosis unlikely. Imp: Poikiloderma vasculare atrophicans. Findings support a diagnosis of poikilodermatous change rather than infiltrative lymphoma or inflammatory parapsoriasis. Plan: 1. Punch biopsy of the trunk to confirm interface dermatitis changes. 2. Baseline CBC, peripheral smear, and LDH to rule out systemic lymphoproliferative involvement. 3. Recommend phototherapy if histology confirms early-stage mycosis fungoides spectrum. 4. Strict sun protection and topical corticosteroids for symptomatic flares. Follow-up in 4 weeks for pathology review.

Diagnosis: Loose body gotini. Plan: X-ray, MRI, rufaa kwa orthopedics kwa ajili ya arthroscopy. Patient: Daktari, najiskia kama kuna jiwe dogo ndani ya goti linanizuia kutembea vizuri.

Subjective: 68-year-old G4P4 female presents with a persistent, golf-ball-sized bulge extruding from the introitus. She reports severe pelvic pressure, difficulty voiding, and fecal urgency requiring digital pressure to evacuate. Symptoms worsened over two years. Objective: Vitals: BP 135/85, HR 76. Pelvic exam confirms total procidentia with the entire uterine corpus, cervix, and both anterior and posterior vaginal walls exteriorized beyond the hymenal ring. No ulceration noted. Assessment: Complete uterine prolapse with anterior and posterior vaginal wall prolapse. The degree of descent confirms full procidentia including both cystocele and rectocele components. Plan: Discussed management options including pessary trial vs. surgical intervention. Patient desires definitive repair. Ordered preoperative urodynamics and scheduled MRI of the pelvic floor. Advised pelvic floor PT for symptomatic management in the interim. Follow up in two weeks to review surgical risks including recurrence and mesh erosion.

Patient: هل هذا خطير؟ ولماذا أحتاج لكل هذه المحاليل؟ Doctor: نعم، لأنكِ فقدتِ الكثير من السوائل والأملاح الضرورية لجسمك، سنبدأ فوراً بتعويض السوائل عبر الوريد وإعطائك أدوية مضادة للقيء للسيطرة على الحالة ومنع مضاعفات الجفاف. يجب أن نبقى في المستشفى لبضعة أيام تحت المراقبة لضمان استقرار نسبة الأملاح في الدم، سأقوم بطلب استشارة قسم التغذية أيضاً لوضع خطة وجبات صغيرة ومقسمة بمجرد تحسن حالتك.

Doctor: Jambo mama, nimeona mtoto ana rangi ya njano sana kwenye ngozi na macho. Je, kuna dawa yoyote uliyompa huyu mtoto tangu azaliwe?
